data.text: Non-flash-based browser tools allow developers to create fast AR prototypes using web technologies like HTML and WebGL. Open Frameworks serves as a C++ middleware library that combines multiple libraries for tracking, rendering, and interaction. Wikitude provides a mobile prototyping tool where computation occurs on backend servers, and it supports both custom and default content.
points: Non-flash-based browser tools allow developers to create fast AR prototypes using HTML or WebGL.
Open Frameworks is a C++ middleware that combines multiple libraries to support tracking, rendering, and interaction.
Wikitude is a mobile browser tool for AR prototyping that performs computation on backend servers.
Wikitude allows for faster prototyping with custom content but can use default content if needed.

data.text: Plugins to existing tools add AR-specific functions to 2D or 3D content authoring tools that may not natively support AR. This method is easy and quick for developers familiar with the host tool, but it can limit user interface design and usually make content dependent on proprietary player software in most cases. Building a system from scratch using low-level software libraries can resolve these limitations.
points: Plugins to existing tools add AR-specific functions to 2D or 3D content authoring tools that do not natively support AR.
This method is easy and quick for developers who know the host tool, but it makes no sense if the tool is unknown.
Using these plugins can limit user interface design, depend on specific hardware configurations, and usually make content dependent on proprietary player software in most cases.
Building a system from scratch using low-level software libraries can resolve the limitations of high-level tools and plugins.

data.text: Standalone authoring tools allow users to create AR experiences without programming experience because they are complete packages that do not depend on any other software. They support scene construction, animation, and interactive behavior. Most provide drag-and-drop interfaces for non-programmers but can also support scripting for more flexibility.
points: Standalone authoring tools allow users to create AR experiences without programming experience.
These tools are complete packages that do not depend on any other software.
They support scene construction, animation, and interactive behavior.
Most provide drag-and-drop interfaces for non-programmers but can also support scripting for more flexibility.

data.text: Augmented reality (AR) software tools and packages are available in four categories based on the programming skill required. Low-level libraries and frameworks require the highest programming skill, while standalone authoring tools require the least. Rapid prototyping tools and plugins to existing systems fall between these extremes.
points: AR software tools are categorized by the programming skill required.
Categories range from high-skill low-level libraries to low-skill standalone authoring tools.
